title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of type 2 diabetes.

HPI
The patient is a 58-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up regarding his type 2 diabetes mellitus. He reports that he has been feeling fatigued lately and notes that his blood glucose readings have been consistently high over the past month. He admits to some difficulty adhering to his current regimen. He has been taking an oral hypoglycemic agent for several years. He denies any recent acute illnesses or changes in his physical activity levels.

Medication List
Metformin 1000mg daily.

Exam
The patient appears in no acute distress. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. Skin is dry with no visible lesions. Vital signs are stable.

Assessment
Type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient is currently experiencing hyperglycemia.

Plan
Continue current dose of metformin. We will monitor his glucose levels more frequently over the next month. The patient was instructed to keep a daily log of his readings and will return in four weeks for a follow-up.
explanations: Diabetes documented as poorly controlled, out of control, or with hyperglycemia is coded to diabetes with hyperglycemia.
Long-term oral hypoglycemic use: add Z79.84.

distractors.why: Hyperglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Z79.84 captures long-term oral hypoglycemic use.
